CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-CAPACITY-FRAMING.statement: Dispute volume doubling is driven by slow/under-resourced ticket handling, so an AI agent auto-answering tickets and auto-fixing bills would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced a systematic bill-calculation defect, causing many bills to be wrong and triggering disputes.

H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: Degraded or incomplete AMI read delivery from the MDMS vendor (nightly export) is causing missing/stale reads, forcing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual meter-reading routes (contracted via MeterWorks) have become incomplete or inaccurate, causing missing reads that trigger estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LOGIC.statement: The billing system's estimate-substitution step (used when no accepted read exists) is itself defective, producing wrong bills independent of which upstream read source is missing.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, affecting 9,200 manual-read accounts — a measurable shortfall in a process step that feeds into estimate substitution and bill issuance.

billing-db's tariff_change_log shows zero records, meaning no tariff/rate change was logged for the relevant period — ruling out a tariff-rate change as the source of wrong bills, independent of read-source or import-rule mechanisms.

Among disputed bills, ACTUAL-read-type bills (1785) outnumber ESTIMATED-read-type bills (1240), so most disputes are not confined to the estimate-substitution path that fires when a read is missing. This points toward a billing-calculation/import defect affecting bills regardless of read source, rather than a pure upstream read-delivery problem.

CRM response-time data (E-04) shows 2440 dispute tickets being resolved within SLA — median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA — despite the reported ticket-volume doubling. This indicates ticket-handling throughput/capacity is not strained, which undercuts the premise that slow/under-resourced response handling is the root cause of the dispute surge.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year, corroborating the already-recorded tool evidence E-02 (billing-db tariff_change_log, 0 records) that ruled out a tariff-rate change as a cause of the wrong bills. As a stakeholder statement it is non-authoritative and adds agreement, not new proof, to a conclusion already established by E-02.

CRM dispute-volume-by-month data (610 Jun, 590 Jul, 1180 Aug, 1260 Sep) confirms a sharp roughly-2x jump beginning in August relative to the June-July baseline, rather than a gradual drift — quantifying the symptom's timing and scale but not its cause.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) attributes the route-completion shortfall already measured in E-01/F-01 to a three-reader staffing gap since July, offering a specific causal explanation for why some routes run late and those accounts receive estimated bills. As a stakeholder statement this is a claim, not a verified fact, and SH-FIELD has a disclosed incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias (attributes problems to staffing) that could inflate this explanation.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document (service contract §4.2) establishes that the utility may request field route priority changes, but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager — it confirms the governance basis for the existing K-DISPATCH constraint rather than speaking to the cause of the billing dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log's lagging_routes query returns per-route completion detail for 14 routes (sample: R-00 at 0.70 completion), providing route-level granularity underneath the aggregate 88% completion rate already recorded in E-01, without linking any specific route to disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-10 (billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle) returns 320 estimated-billing accounts spanning 40 distinct routes, but the record schema exposes only account_id and route — not the read-type, tariff, or import-status fields the pending disputed-bill-pattern and flag-bills work items assumed would be available. This limits what can be directly concluded about the rule-change defect or field-read linkage from this query alone; it only supplies account/route identifiers for further cross-referencing.
